newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen peaking in early 1997 - Merrill Lynch.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen peaking in early 1997 - Merrill Lynch.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock market, sensitive to trends in the U.S., is likely to hit a peak sometime in early 1997, Robert Farrell, senior investment adviser at Merrill Lynch & Co, said on Monday.

"My opinion on Hong Kong is bullish into early 1997, because that pretty much matches the U.S. market opinion. Beyond that I think the market is possibly going to have some repercussions from the U.S. market," he told a financial seminar organised by Merrill Lynch (Asia Pacific) Ltd.
He said U.S. equity markets were overdue for a significant correction and were likely to see lower overall rates of return than the 15 percent annual average of recent years.
The U.S. market was still in a bull market but the risks were high, Farrell said.
He said he feared the coming peak in U.S. equity markets, forecast for late 1996 or early 1997, would be a secular peak as well as a cyclical peak.
Farrell said the Hong Kong market was obviously still in an uptrend and in the short term would move back towards its all-time high, but he was not confident after the early part of 1997.
He said he was more optimistic on many of the emerging markets, which were so exploited and popular two years ago that he had not favoured them.
"Today I think there is a better case for emerging markets in 1997, and I think this could happen even if there is a problem in the U.S. market," he said.
"Markets I like in particular are Malaysia, Singapore, Taiwan and Chile," he said.
Farrell said U.S. investor interest in emerging markets had come full circle.
Emerging market funds were selling in 1993 at a 25 percent premium to net asset values before declining, but were now selling at 25 percent discounts, he added.
